lesson.text: Quick memory: is a box a frame or a shell structure? (A shell.) Boxes are strong, light shells, and every one starts out flat.
A net is a flat shape that folds up into a 3D shape. Open out an empty cereal box carefully, and you will see its net.
A cube has 6 square faces, 12 edges and 8 corners (called vertices). So a net of a cube has 6 squares, joined edge to edge.
Not every 6 squares make a cube. Fold it in your head: each square must land on a different face. A row of 6 wraps round and overlaps, leaving two faces open.
There are 11 different nets of a cube. Here is another one: fold the middle row into a ring, then the two squares above and below close the ends.
A cuboid's net has 6 rectangles: each face has a twin the same size on the opposite side. A square-based pyramid's net is 1 square and 4 triangles.
To make a box: draw the net and add tabs for gluing. Score the fold lines with a ruler. Cut it out, fold it up and glue the tabs. Test it: does it hold and protect what goes inside?
Try it in the world: lay a net of a cube flat on the ground with 6 blocks, and fold it in your head. Then build the cube itself, 3 blocks high!

exercises.prompt: How many faces does a cube have?
exercises.hint: Count: top, bottom, and the sides.
exercises.explain: A cube has 6 faces: top, bottom, front, back, left and right.

exercises.prompt: A net is a flat shape that folds into a 3D shape.
exercises.hint: Think of the opened-out cereal box.
exercises.explain: True: a net is flat, and folds up into a 3D shape.

exercises.prompt: What shape are the faces of a cube?
exercises.explain: Every face of a cube is a square.

exercises.prompt: Will this net fold into a cube?
exercises.hint: Fold the middle row into a ring, then close the ends.
exercises.explain: Yes: the row of 4 makes a ring, and the squares above and below close the two ends.

exercises.prompt: Will this net fold into a cube?
exercises.explain: No: a row of 6 wraps round and the last two squares land on top of the first two, leaving two faces open.

exercises.prompt: Will this net of 6 squares fold into a cube?
exercises.hint: Look for four squares meeting at one corner.
exercises.explain: No: four squares meet round one corner, which cannot happen on a cube, so two of them overlap.

exercises.prompt: How many edges does a cube have?
exercises.hint: Count the edges round the top, round the bottom, then the upright ones.
exercises.explain: 4 round the top, 4 round the bottom and 4 upright: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 edges.

exercises.prompt: Which shapes make the net of a square-based pyramid?
exercises.hint: What is its base, and what are its sides?
exercises.explain: A square base, and 4 triangles that meet at the top.

exercises.prompt: Which net folds into a cube?
exercises.hint: Fold each one in your head: does any face get two squares?
exercises.explain: The one with a row of 4 and one square above and below: the row makes a ring and those two close its ends.

exercises.prompt: Build a net of a cube on the board: 6 squares that would fold into a cube.
exercises.hint: Try a row of 4 squares, then add one square above it and one below it.
exercises.explain: A row of 4 with one square above and one below (like a cross) folds into a cube; so do 10 other nets.

exercises.prompt: In a cuboid's net, how many rectangles are there?
exercises.hint: A cuboid has as many faces as a cube.
exercises.explain: A cuboid has 6 faces, so its net has 6 rectangles, in 3 matching pairs.

exercises.prompt: Why do box nets have tabs?
exercises.hint: What joins one face to the next?
exercises.explain: Tabs are flaps with glue on them that hold the faces together.

exercises.prompt: How many corners (vertices) does a cube have?
exercises.hint: Count the corners on the top, then on the bottom.
exercises.explain: 4 corners on the top and 4 on the bottom: 4 + 4 = 8 vertices.

exercises.prompt: Four squares of a net are in a row. Add 2 more squares to make a net of a cube.
exercises.hint: The row folds into a ring; the two new squares must close its two open ends.
exercises.explain: Put one square above the row and one below it (on any of the 4 squares): they close the ring's two ends.

exercises.prompt: There are 11 different nets of a cube.
exercises.explain: True: there are 11 different ways to unfold a cube into a net.

exercises.prompt: Fold this net into a cube. Which face is opposite A?
exercises.hint: In a straight line of squares, the ones two apart end up opposite each other.
exercises.explain: A, B and C are in a line: folded up, A and C are two apart, so they end up on opposite sides.

exercises.prompt: Match each 3D shape to its net.
exercises.hint: Count the faces of each shape and think about their shapes.
exercises.explain: A cube's net is 6 squares, a cuboid's is 6 rectangles in matching pairs, and a square-based pyramid's is 1 square and 4 triangles.

exercises.prompt: Put the steps of making a box in order.
items: Fold it up and glue the tabs.
Draw the net and add tabs.
Score the fold lines with a ruler.
exercises.hint: You can only score and cut what you have drawn, and only test what you have made.
exercises.explain: Draw the net with tabs, score the fold lines while it is flat, cut it out, fold it and glue the tabs, then test that it holds and protects what goes inside.
